purpose: Fluoxetine is used to treat depression, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), panic attacks, and certain eating disorders like bulimia. It can also help with premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). Your doctor may prescribe it for other conditions as well.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called serotonin to help regulate your mood, emotions, and sleep. Fluoxetine works by keeping more serotonin available in your brain by blocking it from being reabsorbed too quickly. Think of it like keeping the 'feel-good' chemical around longer so your brain can use it more effectively.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, trouble sleeping or feeling drowsy, dry mouth, sweating, nervousness or feeling jittery, decreased appetite, and sexual side effects like reduced sex drive. Most of these tend to improve after the first few weeks as your body adjusts.
warnings: Fluoxetine may increase thoughts of suicide in some people, especially in children, teens, and young adults — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal-like symptoms. Avoid taking it with certain other medications, especially MAOIs, as this can cause a dangerous reaction called serotonin syndrome. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have liver problems.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 20 mg once a day, taken in the morning. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time if needed, up to a maximum of 80 mg per day depending on your condition. It can take 4 to 6 weeks before you feel the full benefit, so be patient and keep taking it as directed.
